section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section contains the opening header of the maamar, including the date and Torah portion.
section.t: With the help of Heaven.
Shabbat Parshat Miketz,
Shabbat Chanukah, 5748*

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section questions why Chanukah begins on the 25th of Kislev, the miracle of the oil, rather than on the 24th, the day of the military victory.
section.t: "And You, in Your abundant mercies, stood for them in their time of distress... You delivered the mighty into the hands of the weak, and the many into the hands of the few..."
And my father-in-law, the Rebbe, precisely analyzes in his maamar beginning with the words "Zeh"
(which was said fifty years ago),
[saying that] the primary miracle
(of Chanukah)
is the miracle of the victory in the war, which occurred on the 24th of Kislev,
and this was even the cause of the miracle of the flask of oil that occurred on the 25th of Kislev,
[as it is stated in the Gemara:
"When the Chashmonaim prevailed and defeated them
(specifically then)
they found one flask of oil... a miracle was performed with it, and they lit from it for eight days."]
Why, then, did they establish the beginning of the days of Chanukah on the 25th of Kislev, when the miracle of the lights occurred, and not on the 24th of Kislev?

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the Rebbe's precise question differs from other discourses because he holds that Chanukah was established for both miracles, yet the days still begin on the 25th.
section.t: One could say,
that this precise point in the maamar—the reason they established Chanukah on the 25th of Kislev and not on the 24th of Kislev—
is unlike the precise point in several other discourses
(including also discourses that begin with the words "Zeh"),
which ask: Why was Chanukah established for the miracle of the flask of oil and not for the miracle of the victory in the war?
The explanation is,
that in those aforementioned discourses, they follow the opinion
that the festival of Chanukah was established
(only)
for the miracle of the lights,
and therefore they ask that ostensibly the main thing is the victory in the war,
so why did they make the secondary thing primary and the primary thing secondary?
But in this maamar, it follows the opinion
that the establishment of the festival of Chanukah is also because of the miracle of the victory in the war,
to the extent that the thanksgiving in "Al HaNissim" is
(primarily)
for this miracle
[and the thanksgiving for the miracle of the flask of oil is through the lighting of the Chanukah candle].
Therefore, the precise point in this maamar is this: that the days of Chanukah
[which were established also for the miracle of the victory in the war,
and furthermore,
this matter is
(ostensibly)
the primary miracle,
to the extent that it was even the cause of the miracle of the flask of oil]
begin on the 25th of Kislev, when the miracle of the lights occurred, and not on the 24th of Kislev.
